_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
1/8 5:50AM - Who’s ready for some prime midweek turns? After a 6 inch storm, we dropped ropes on more than 240 acres yesterday, and we’re stoked to be skiing and riding across 585 acres of open terrain today! For your Thursday, you'll find your way down 92 trails, 68 of which were smoothed out overnight. 9 lifts are scheduled to spin at 9AM with no anticipated delays. It's shaping up to be yet another stellar day here at Stratton. Catch you on the slopes!

The park scene is coming to life with a 13-foot Halfpipe open and firing on East Byrnes Side with 6 features ready to ride. Tyrolinne is also open with 7 features to keep the park laps rolling. 

Operations Update: Snowmaking has been extra active over the past few days, concentrating efforts on Stevek, World Cup, Churchill Downs, Lower Middlebrook, Upper Down Easter, Black Bear, Janeway Junction, Upper and Lower West Meadow, Lower Kidderbrook, Daniel Webster, Big Ben, Upper and Lower East Meadow, and Lower Wanderer. Forecasted warmer temperatures and the chance of rain will temporarily put guns on hold beginning mid-week through this coming weekend. Once cold temperatures return, snowmaking will resume with the next round targeting Upper and Lower East Meadow, Bear Down, Upper Kidderbrook, Free Fall, Upper Standard, Rime Line, Supertrail and Big Ben. A brief warm-up is nothing new for our Operations Team, who will continue working around the clock to deliver the best possible conditions. Be sure to stay tuned to the Mountain Report for more snowmaking and operational updates to come.

Safety Tip: Always ski or ride with a friend in the glades. 

Spots have opened up this weekend on January 10 for a once-in-a-lifetime winter dining experience! Our Snowcat Dinners offer a ride in a snowcat to our Mid-Mountain Lodge, where a seasonal welcome beverage and hors d’oeuvres lead into a candlelit, six-course dinner crafted by our culinary team. If you can’t make it Saturday, we have plenty more dates available this winter season; Book now to secure your spot!

Discover the thrill of skiing or snowboarding with Stratton Mountain's Learn to Ski or Ride Program. This step-by-step program is designed to help you master the slopes—and reward you with a 25/26 Stratton Select Pass, to ride out the rest of the season, upon completion.

Looking to progress this season? Stratton’s Camps and Clinics offer targeted skill development, expert coaching, and a strong sense of community for skiers and snowboarders. From women’s programs to freestyle, snowboard, and advanced clinics, each offers a supportive, goal focused environment to help you make the most of the season, with programs offered all throughout the winter. 

Stay and relish the Green Mountains! Stratton Real Estate is here to help with all your real estate needs. Make your sweet escape a reality.

Reliable cars are the name of the game; that is why we trust Oliver Subaru and Ford. Made for all seasons and all families, check out Oliver Ford and Oliver Subaru for year-round reliability.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report: The snow tap is on! Another storm has arrived, dropping off 9 inches of new snow overnight with another few inches forecast while lifts are spinning today. We’ve received over four feet of snow in the last week, greatly improving conditions and allowing us to open most of our frontside terrain. The skiing and riding should be great today, with cold temperatures keeping the snow light and fluffy. Summit Express opened for the season yesterday, providing access to multiple trails, including Dynamite and Headwall Forest. We hope to have Summit spinning again today following avalanche mitigation work this morning. Expect some delays on lifts and terrain this morning as mitigation work takes place. To reach Summit you must take the Sunrise chairlift – there is currently no access from the top of Apex Express. Keep your eyes peeled for unmarked hazards, especially in the trees, and stay out of closed terrain. Ducking ropes into closed terrain will cost you your pass for 30 days at all Ikon Pass resorts. Enjoy the new snow and have a thrilling Thursday at Solitude!

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Good Morning Skiers and Riders! This is Eli with your 5 am snow report for Thursday, January  8th . Remember the easiest way to get up to date information is on the Ikon Pass app or website.  

At Mid Mountain, we’ve had 3 new inches of snow in the past 24 hours, with 3 inches falling since the mountain closed yesterday.  

At the Summit, we’ve had 4 new inches of snow in the past 24 hours, with 4 inches falling since the mountain closed yesterday.  

Our Mid mountain base is 27 inches, the temperature is 24 degrees, the winds are 6 miles per hour from the southwest, and it’s currently snowing. 

The Summit base is 39 inches, the temperature is 17 degrees, the winds 11 miles per hour from the south/southwest. 

The base temperature is 27 degrees.  

We will be skiing and riding on 19 lifts, 103 runs, and 1,348 acres on packed powder snow.  Night skiing and riding will be open tonight from 5:30-8:30pm with 4 runs and 1,100 vertical feet off of Christie Peak Express. 

Musicfest at Steamboat continues today with plenty of free music to enjoy. This afternoon, head down to Steamboat Square for incredible live music set against a classic mountain backdrop. The first band starts playing at 12pm, head to steamboat.com/events for the full lineup. 

Stay in the know with the Ikon Pass App. Find it in the app store on your mobile device and get lift and trail statuses, conditions updates, and more.  

If you are thinking of exploring outside the ski area boundaries, and don’t know exactly where you are going, don’t go.  

Ski and Ride with Care and we will see you on the mountain!

Wednesday, January 7, 2026 6:10 AM – It will be a crisp winter day with temperatures in the low 20s with a breeze and gusts that may impact lift operations. Cloud cover will vary, so expect a mix of sun and clouds. We are expecting 22 lifts to operate today with fun turns off of the summit. Check out Christmas Bowl for pockets that still have some fresh snow. The Panorama Gondola is expected to be on wind hold to start off the day. Enjoy the snow safely by looking out for one another. Please ski with a partner, keep them in sight, and avoid tree wells. Emergency hotline: 760.934.0611

Conditions: Packed powder with powder stashes still to be found.
Visibility: Good visibility with variable cloud cover throughout the day.
Lift status: 22 lifts are expected to operate. Gusts may impact lift operations, The Panorama Gondola is expected to be on wind hold to start off the day.
Safety: Please avoid tree wells and try to land feet first when falling. Always ski and ride in a group and keep them in sight. Learn more about tree wells and Snow Immersion Suffocation. Please give heavy machinery space. Our on-mountain emergency hotline is: 760.934.0611
Road Conditions: The highway is clear, however there are still spots that may be snowy/icy around town, so drive with caution. Check our Road Conditions page for the latest status.

Wednesday January 7, 2026 -- 8:30AM 
Expect all lifts to operate on time under a splattering of clouds today. Winds are expected to pick up throughout the day but shouldn't affect operations. A cold, mostly dry, system will brush by to our north this evening leaving cold temps in its wake tomorrow. High pressure then sets in until at least mid-month.

1/8/26:  5:00 AM Update: : It’s another wintry morning at Crystal Mountain with temps in the teens and a solid refresh of low density snow around the mountain. On top of the feet of snow we’ve received this week, this parting gift from Ullr will make for some all-time turns out there. Our main area saw a lot of traffic yesterday, but freshies still abound -- especially out in Southback. Winds have picked up and it’s chilly outside, so make sure to dress warm because powder is on the menu.

While you may not receive an immediate reply, the cancellation will be processed. The Crystal Mountain Contact center cannot process these cancellations.

1/7/26 1:13 PM: Southback is now open. Northway will remain closed today. 

Uphill Travel Status: Uphill travel is NOT permitted. Uphill Status is subject to closure at any time, and travelers must check Uphill Status lights before departure.

⚠️ Snow Immersion Warning ⚠️
Deep, unconsolidated snow conditions today create a high risk of snow immersion suffocation, especially in trees, steep terrain, and terrain traps. A fall into deep snow can make self-rescue extremely difficult and time is critical. Stay safe out there:
  • Always ski or ride with a partner in sight
  • Stop frequently and regroup
  • Avoid skiing alone in trees or deep features
  • If a partner goes down, respond immediately
  • Carry rescue gear and know how to use it

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
January 8th, 6:20 AM
Good morning riders and skiers! This warmer weather has delivered some phenomenal snow conditions the past few days. The forecast calls for partial clouds with comfortable temps in the upper 20's at the summit and low to mid 30's at the base by the afternoon. Come enjoy dreamy groomers and soft packed powder conditions across the mountain. Snowmaking is on pause today until temps become more conducive.

We will be getting down on 450 skiable acres served by 12 lifts and 108 open trails, with 39 of those getting a fresh corduroy overnight. Check out fan favorite Jester to Spring Fling for a top-tier corduroy experience! Castlerock lift will be spinning today from 9:00 AM - 3:45 PM, plus, North Lynx is scheduled to run starting today 9:00 AM -3:45 PM as well! All natural terrain is suggested for experts only as base coverage is thin and conditions are variable. Inverness and Racer's Edge will be closed today for racing events.

Operations have moved back to weekday hours, which means GMX kicks things off, loading at 8:00 AM. Followed by all other scheduled lifts at 9:00 AM. This weekend, look forward to Ikon early ups on Super Bravo loading at 7:30 AM- for Ikon pass holders looking to score some fresh cord and untouched powder before lifts open to the public. Sugarbush offers a wide range of freestyle parks, whether you’re just starting out or training for competitions, we’ve got you covered. At Mt. Ellen, Riemergasse offers 80 of the finest features on the East Coast, while Lincoln Peak is home to two mini parks featuring 12 creative elements. Sugar Run made its season debut yesterday with 27 features including 3 jumps, bringing out total feature count to 119!

Sharpen Your Swing This Winter! Join PGA Pro Roger King Jan 12th from 5:00 PM - 7:00 PM at the SIM Suites in the SHaRC for exclusive winter golf lessons. Using state-of-the-art simulators, you'll get personalized tips and real-time feedback to improve your swing, accuracy, and overall game. Check out all of our winter events!

All uphill routes are open at both Lincoln Peak and Mt. Ellen, check out our uphill travel policy for more info.

Bonjour Tremblant!

Spend the day with us on the mountain! Mild temperatures and beautifully groomed terrain make it the perfect time to get outside and enjoy the snow! Thanks to the hard work of our dedicated team, the mountain is in great shape, offering something for everyone—from carving turns to making memories with family. 

First Tracks: Access to designated lifts, on North and South side, as early as 7:45 am.

Terrain Park fans will be happy to hear that all 4 parks are open.

Alpine Touring is available today, with access to 15 sections across the mountain.

We can’t wait to welcome you for an unforgettable day on the mountain. See you on the slopes!

Mountain safety tip of the week: Be careful when using the ski lifts.
Knowing how to board ski lifts is essential to ensure the safety of all users.
 
Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
